newsitem.title: UK: UK accepts pledges from rivals on Lloyds Chemists.
newsitem.headline: UK accepts pledges from rivals on Lloyds Chemists.

text.p: Britain's Department of Trade and Industry said on Friday it has accepted undertakings from pharmacists UniChem and Germany's Gehe AG to sell off parts of Lloyds Chemists if either of them acquire the company.
"UniChem and GEHE have each identified a number of potential firm buyers for the businesses they are required to divest. These have been approved by the Minister," said the DTI.
The decision cleared the way for UniChem to renew its bid, valuing the company at some 658 million pounds.

Lloyds Chemists, the country's largest high street pharmacy chain, is the target of two rival bids which both technically lapsed when they were referred to Britain's Monopolies and Mergers Commission in March.
UniChem's renewed offer consists of 16 new shares and 926p cash for every 10 LLoyds shares. GEHE's lapsed offer was an all cash bid pitched at a cash 500 pence per share offer.

UniChem also said it had identified cost savings and revenue benefits "conservatively" estimated to total more than 15 million in the 12 months after the acquisition and in excess of 20 million annually thereafter.

If either UniChem or GEHE is successful in its bid to acquire Lloyds they must sell off the specified businesses within three months of the completed merger, said John Taylor, minister for corporate and consumer affairs at the DTI.
UniChem has pledged to sell the wholesaling businesses operated by Lloyds from the depots at Cambridge, Carlisle, Coulsdon, Derby, Glasgow and York.
In addition to these, GEHE has promised the authorities that it would sell LLoyds' depot business at Belfast.
